chapter: Bolden and the road to New Orleans
title: What Bolden looked like and how he practiced
summary: Ory describes Bolden's hair, build and loud practising on the sidewalk step.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Oh. What do you look like Bolden? What kind of a man was he? Can you describe him physically?

Yeah, he was kind of on a Moroni style look, you know. His hair went black and more exactly red. I see. Red and... And black. And they never combed it, it was always just way out of a cutty loose there. Was he big or small? Well, it's the time I saw him then, he was the size of, I say, Jim Robinson, but not quite as tall.
Strong man. Strong, yeah, strong man.
No, brown skinned. Brown skinned. And he never practiced in the house, he practiced on the box step out in the street, on the sidewalk.

He blows so loud he blew everyone out of the house when he practiced. Then he get out on the sidewalk and on the step and practice the tune and the kids are all gang around, King Baldwin, King Baldwin. Girls? Girls, boys and kids. Everything. Yeah. School kids and all.
How old was he when he came into the store there, do you think?
To his house. Oh, to his house. Oh, I never know Bolden, right age, you know.
But he was a grown man, actually.
Oh, yeah. Well, what? Do you think he was in his 40s?
Well, yeah, he was about 37, 37 and 40.
What did his face look like?
Well, he had a round face. Plump or? Yeah, plump and not very tall. He was well big but not a tall man, you know. Anybody that you know that resembles him at all?
Did he have a spread nose, sort of like the one you describe as a meat nose? Meat nose, no.
